findings.title: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49 path traversal
findings.description: A path normalisation flaw in Apache 2.4.49 allows files outside the document root to be read and, with mod_cgi enabled, remote code execution.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to Apache 2.4.51 or later (2.4.50 fix was incomplete, see CVE-2021-42013) and set 'Require all denied' on the filesystem root.

findings.title: vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoored release
findings.description: The vsftpd 2.3.4 source archive distributed in mid-2011 contained a backdoor that opens a root shell when a username ending in ':)' is sent.
findings.remediation: Replace vsftpd with a current release from a trusted source and verify package signatures.

findings.title: SMBv1 enabled (MS17-010 exposure)
findings.description: SMBv1 is enabled. Unpatched hosts are exposed to MS17-010 (EternalBlue), which was used by WannaCry and NotPetya for wormable lateral movement.
findings.remediation: Apply MS17-010, disable SMBv1 and block TCP 445 between workstation segments.
findings.evidence: 445/tcp SMBv1 | banner: SMBv1 dialect NT LM 0.12 - Windows 7 Professional 7601 Service Pack 1

findings.title: Tomcat Manager application exposed
findings.description: The Tomcat Manager is reachable from the network. It is a frequent target for default or weak credentials, after which a malicious WAR file can be deployed.
findings.remediation: Restrict /manager to localhost or a management VLAN, remove default users from tomcat-users.xml and enforce strong credentials.

findings.title: Redis accepts unauthenticated commands
findings.description: Redis answered PING without authentication. Unauthenticated Redis can be abused to read data or write files such as SSH authorized_keys or cron jobs.
findings.remediation: Bind Redis to localhost, enable protected-mode and requirepass or ACLs, and firewall port 6379.

findings.title: Telnet remote access in cleartext
findings.description: Telnet sends credentials and session data unencrypted, so anyone on the network path can capture them.
findings.remediation: Disable Telnet and use SSH with key-based authentication.

findings.title: OpenSSH username enumeration
findings.description: OpenSSH before 7.7 responds differently to valid and invalid usernames during public-key authentication, letting an attacker enumerate accounts before password attacks.
findings.remediation: Upgrade OpenSSH to 7.7 or later, disable password authentication and rate-limit SSH.

findings.title: End-of-life MySQL server
findings.description: MySQL releases before 5.7 no longer receive security fixes, so known vulnerabilities stay unpatched.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to a supported MySQL release and restrict 3306 to application servers.

findings.title: RDP exposed to the network
findings.description: Remote Desktop is reachable. Exposed RDP is a common target for password spraying and, on unpatched systems, for BlueKeep-class vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Put RDP behind a VPN or RD Gateway, enforce NLA and MFA, and apply account lockout.
